# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for the doctor check `node_data_dir_single_writer` (DESIGN.md §7.1) against input/.
# How to read this file: tests/fixtures/doctor/node_layout/expect.json.
#
# THIS CASE: A FOREIGN monerod HOLDS THE DATA DIR, named on its own argv.
# input/proc/8421/cmdline is `/usr/bin/monerod\0--data-dir\0/var/lib/monero\0--non-interactive\0` --
# NUL-separated with a trailing NUL, exactly as the kernel writes /proc/<pid>/cmdline. THE FILE
# CONTAINS NUL BYTES: a text editor will corrupt it. Regenerate rather than edit (see
# tests/fixtures/README.md).
# /var/lib/monero is upstream's own systemd/conf template default (utils/conf/monerod.conf:1,
# utils/systemd/monerod.service:1-20), i.e. what Arch's system unit uses -- the realistic foreign
# holder of §1.2. _settings points node.data_dir at the same path so the comparison is meaningful.
# THE PATH DOES NOT EXIST ON THIS MACHINE, deliberately: §2i says the argv path must "resolve to the
# same canonical path" as node.data_dir, and std::fs::canonicalize FAILS on a missing path. A detector
# that canonicalizes unconditionally errors out here and reports the data dir free -- on a machine
# where the data dir has not been created yet, which is every machine before the first `node up`. It
# must fall back to lexical normalisation.
# DECOYS IN THE TREE, each there to make a sloppy scan fail:
#   pid 1     /sbin/init      -- a process with no --data-dir at all
#   pid 2451  monero-wallet-rpc -- a MONERO binary that is not monerod and holds no data dir; a scan
#             matching on the substring "monero" in argv[0] reports it and names the wrong pid
#   (__free adds pid 9001 `monerod-not-really`, which a prefix match on "monerod" would catch)
#
# WHAT THIS FIXTURE CANNOT DRIVE, AND MUST NOT BE READ AS COVERING: §2i's SECOND probe, the
# fcntl(F_GETLK) test on <data-dir>/lmdb/lock.mdb. A held POSIX record lock is live kernel state, not
# a file, so no fixture can supply one. §2i's own named test does it instead: a forked child holds an
# fcntl READ lock (F_RDLCK, l_start 0, l_len 1) -- the lock a real monerod holds, because
# mdb_env_share_locks downgrades the setup-time exclusive one
# (external/db_drivers/liblmdb/mdb.c:5022-5057) -- and data_dir_in_use must return Some(child_pid).
# THE QUERY TYPE IS LOAD-BEARING THERE: only an F_WRLCK query conflicts with a held read lock, so an
# F_GETLK{F_RDLCK} probe -- the natural reading of "is this file locked?" -- reports a LIVE data dir
# as free and `node up` starts a second writer on the LMDB (§1.2). And flock() is a separate namespace
# entirely: an flock probe succeeds while monerod holds the environment.
# status `fail`, severity `error`: two monerod on one LMDB corrupt it. THE DETAIL MUST NAME THE PID,
# because §7.1's fix column for this row IS "detail names the PID" -- there is no command to run.
# `fixable` false, class D: the doctor never stops a daemon it did not start (§7).
# NOTE that `node up` treats the SAME probe differently (§2i): a holder whose pid equals our own
# unit's MainPID is exit 0 "already running", not a refusal. This check is report-only and does not
# make that distinction; whether it should is the Phase 2 doctor agent's call.
# EDITED BY THE PHASE 2 DOCTOR AGENT (DESIGN.md §8 hands this directory to it): see
# decisions/phase2-doctor.md for the reason, stated case by case.
# ADDED `_probe.monerod_installed`: every check in the `node` group reports
# skip:monerod_not_installed when /usr/bin/monerod is absent, which is §4b's GREEN row for
# this machine and §7.1's "every check whose precondition is missing reports skip:<reason>".
# No file under input/ can carry that fact, so the harness states it here.
